newsitem.title: UK: Kvaerner mulls winding up Kirkenes yard.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner mulls winding up Kirkenes yard.

text.p: Norwegian shipbuilding and engineering firm Kvaerner ASA said on Thursday its Kvaerner Kimek unit would start talks with employees to wind up its present shipyard operations in Kirkenes, northern Norway.
Kvaerner attributed the move to a weaker-than-expected market for work on Russian ships.
A wind-up of operations at the loss-making business would affect about a third of the site's 130-strong workforce, a spokesman said.
"We're not talking about huge numbers," he said, noting that the other two-thirds of the staff were currently laid off.
The spokesman added that it was too early to count the cost of the move, noting that the board would make a final decision on the site's fate at a meeting on May 28.
"We're going to assess fully then any subsequential cost," he said.
Kvaerner planned to retain and maintain the Kirkenes facility and explore the possibility of new, profitable operations, if market opportunities should change.

"Two-thirds of the staff are currently laid off and, as far as we can see, it will take between two and three years before we can again find profitable operations which will provide full, or almost full, employment at the yard," Kvaerner said in a statement released here.
